scope: scripts/qualify_hardware_changes.py on a frozen Debug build of 16cca44 (D:\wp\b27), 127/127 steps, in an owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 with an added CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 on one subnet and two DI 16x24VDC HF modules in the CPU rack: hardware_add, hardware_attributes (Comment, Author), hardware_replace (firmware V1.0 and V2.0), hardware_port_connect and hardware_port_disconnect (X1 ports of the two CPUs) and hardware_delete (the rack's last module), each applied with checkpoint, device compile and save, asserted previews and change_status; hardware_inspect items with complete attribute values, addresses, channels, ports and subnet membership, device_inventory rows and every PLC's program exports differ in exactly the intended keys, with TIA's mirrored module comment and port cable defaults recorded as side effects; a fresh owned Portal reopen shows the identical state; one change per kind restored from its checkpoint equals its pre-change state (hardware_add and a port connection before the reopen, because generated CPU security is scratch-only and a second link would form a ring). Typed refusals (ObjectExists, CatalogItemNotFound, UnsupportedAttribute, HardwareNotFound, InvalidRequest, SoftwareBearingHardware, UnsupportedCapability, BuiltInHardware, PreviewMismatch, StaleRevision) change nothing.
limitations: Two CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 and DI 16x24VDC HF modules only; ET 200SP/MP, HMI, drive and GSD devices are not added, because an unassigned IO device does not compile on its own.
hardware_replace only between firmware versions that keep the addresses; acceptLoss and address-changing replacements are not exercised.
A module deletion that leaves a gap in an S7-1500 rack and a second link between the same two CPUs (a ring without media redundancy) fail the device compile.
Engineering only; nothing is downloaded and no physical topology is observed.
